notes.front: What is extended detection and response (XDR)?
notes.back: An approach that correlates signals across security products, such as email, endpoint, identity and cloud apps, to detect and respond to attacks as a whole.
notes.explanation: Attacks often cross from one area to another, so tools that share signals see the full chain.
notes.example: Like several neighbourhood watch groups sharing one radio channel, so a burglar seen in one street is expected in the next.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “Advanced threat protection”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Defender XDR?
notes.back: Microsoft’s unified pre- and post-breach enterprise defence suite, coordinating detection, prevention, investigation and response across endpoints, identities, email and applications.
notes.explanation: Bringing signals from several products together shows how an attack entered, what it affected and how to stop it.
notes.example: Like a hospital where every ward shares one patient record, rather than each keeping its own notes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender XDR services, “Describe Microsoft Defender XDR services”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the Microsoft Defender portal?
notes.back: Microsoft’s unified security operations portal, bringing Defender XDR, Microsoft Sentinel and Defender for Cloud into one place to monitor, investigate and respond.
notes.explanation: Each Defender product is experienced through it, under its own node in the left navigation.
notes.example: Like a single airport control tower that replaced separate towers for each runway.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender XDR services, “The Microsoft Defender portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender XDR, what is the combined incidents queue?
notes.back: The queue where related alerts, suspicious events and affected assets from every suite product are grouped automatically into single incidents.
notes.explanation: Analysts see the whole attack story, from entry point to affected assets, instead of chasing alerts in separate consoles.
notes.example: Like a newsroom desk that merges reports from several correspondents into one story about the same event.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender XDR services, “Combined incidents queue”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender XDR, what is automatic attack disruption?
notes.back: A capability that spots attacks in progress from high-fidelity signals and contains them in real time, without waiting for a person.
notes.explanation: It correlates signals into one high-confidence incident and identifies the assets the attacker controls.
notes.example: Like a circuit breaker that trips on its own the instant a fault is detected.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender XDR services, “Automatic attack disruption”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender XDR, what is self-healing for devices, identities and mailboxes?
notes.back: Automatic remediation that returns the assets affected by an incident to a secure state, where possible.
notes.explanation: It uses AI-powered automatic actions and playbooks across the suite, reducing manual recovery work.
notes.example: Like a cleaning crew that restores every room a flood touched once the leak is stopped.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender XDR services, “Self-healing for compromised devices, user identities, and mailboxes”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
introduces: self-healing for devices, identities and mailboxes

notes.front: What is Microsoft Defender for Office 365?
notes.back: A cloud-based email and collaboration security service that protects against threats such as phishing and malware arriving by email, links, attachments or collaboration tools.
notes.explanation: It covers tools such as Outlook, SharePoint and Teams, and adds investigation, hunting and remediation.
notes.example: Like a post room that X-rays parcels and checks return addresses before anything reaches a desk.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Office 365, what is Safe Attachments?
notes.back: A feature that opens email attachments in a virtual environment to see what they do, after the usual virus scan.
notes.explanation: This opening-to-observe is called detonation, and it is an extra layer against malware.
notes.example: Like a bomb squad opening a suspicious package inside a blast chamber.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Prevent and detect”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Office 365, what is Safe Links?
notes.back: A scanning feature that protects the organisation from malicious links used in phishing and other attacks.
notes.explanation: It targets the link in a message, where Safe Attachments targets the file.
notes.example: Like a doorman who checks the address on an invitation before letting you follow it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Prevent and detect”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Office 365, what is attack simulation training?
notes.back: A feature that lets admins run realistic, simulated attacks in their own organisation to find and train vulnerable users.
notes.explanation: The aim is to train people before a real attack harms the organisation.
notes.example: Like an unannounced fire drill that shows who does not know the way out.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Prevent and detect”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Office 365, what is Threat Explorer?
notes.back: A near real-time tool, also just called Explorer, for investigating and responding to email threats, such as seeing detected malware.
notes.explanation: From it, admins can also start an automated investigation and response process.
notes.example: Like a search console over the post room’s logbook, where you can also order a recall.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Investigate”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Office 365, what does the campaigns feature do?
notes.back: It identifies and categorises coordinated phishing and malware email attacks.
notes.explanation: It gives the overall picture of an email attack faster and more completely than a person could.
notes.example: Like a detective linking a string of burglaries to one gang, rather than filing each as a separate crime.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Investigate”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is zero-hour auto purge (ZAP)?
notes.back: A Defender for Office 365 feature that retroactively detects and neutralises phishing, spam or malware messages already delivered to Exchange Online mailboxes.
notes.explanation: It acts after delivery, when a message is found to be malicious later.
notes.example: Like a food recall that pulls a product off shelves after it has been sold.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Respond”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is automated investigation and response (AIR)?
notes.back: Capabilities that investigate well-known threats automatically and take action, without an analyst running every step.
notes.explanation: Defender for Endpoint calls its version automated investigation and remediation, and says it significantly reduces alert volume, which frees analysts for harder threats.
notes.example: Like a triage nurse who handles routine cases and passes only the complex ones to the doctor.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Office 365, “Respond”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Defender for Endpoint?
notes.back: A platform that protects enterprise endpoints, such as laptops, phones, tablets, routers and firewalls, by preventing, detecting, investigating and responding to advanced threats.
notes.explanation: It uses technology built into Windows and Microsoft cloud services.
notes.example: Like a guard posted in every office of a building, not just at the front door.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Endpoint, what is attack surface reduction?
notes.back: The first layer of defence: capabilities that make sure configuration is set properly and exploit mitigations are applied, so attacks are resisted.
notes.explanation: It includes network protection and web protection, which control access to malicious addresses and domains.
notes.example: Like bricking up unused doors and windows so a burglar has fewer ways in.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Endpoint, what is next-generation protection?
notes.back: Protection designed to catch all kinds of emerging threats, built around Microsoft Defender Antivirus.
notes.explanation: It adds behaviour-based and real-time antivirus, cloud-delivered protection and dedicated updates.
notes.example: Like a vaccine programme that is updated as new strains appear.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is endpoint detection and response (EDR)?
notes.back: Near real-time, actionable detection of advanced attacks on endpoints, letting analysts prioritise alerts, see a breach’s full scope and respond.
notes.explanation: Because detections are near real time and actionable, analysts can take response actions to remediate threats.
notes.example: Like a security camera with a guard watching: it catches what the locks did not stop.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Endpoint”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps?
notes.back: A cross-SaaS security solution that gives visibility, data controls and threat protection for cloud apps.
notes.explanation: It goes beyond a traditional cloud access security broker, adding posture management and app-to-app protection.
notes.example: Like a building manager who tracks every tenant, their keys and what they store.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a cloud access security broker (CASB)?
notes.back: A gatekeeper that brokers real-time access between an organisation’s users and the cloud resources they use.
notes.explanation: Its functions include discovering cloud app use, protecting against app threats, information protection and compliance.
notes.example: Like a customs post between the office and the internet’s cloud services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is SaaS security posture management (SSPM)?
notes.back: Surfacing misconfigurations in connected SaaS apps and recommending specific actions to strengthen each app’s security.
notes.explanation: Teams are spared researching best practice for every app separately.
notes.example: Like a checklist per rental flat, telling the landlord which locks each one still needs.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Defender for Cloud Apps, what is app governance?
notes.back: Visibility and control over OAuth apps and their access, protecting data exchanged between apps.
notes.explanation: OAuth apps often hold wide permissions to act on a user’s behalf, which makes them open to compromise.
notes.example: Like auditing every spare key you have handed to tradespeople, and taking back those no longer needed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “App to app protection with app governance”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Defender for Identity?
notes.back: A cloud-based solution that uses signals from identity infrastructure, such as on-premises Active Directory, to detect identity threats and report easily exploited identity issues.
notes.explanation: It also takes signals from Microsoft Entra ID, so it helps protect hybrid environments.
notes.example: Like an alarm wired into the building’s key-cutting room, watching who copies which keys.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In identity security, what is lateral movement?
notes.back: An attacker moving from one compromised account or system to others inside the network, to gain control of more sensitive users.
notes.explanation: Defender for Identity treats it as one stage of the attack chain it detects.
notes.example: Like a thief who gets into one flat and then uses its balcony to reach the neighbours’.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Detect threats, using real-time analytics and data intelligence”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management?
notes.back: A risk-based service that finds, assesses, prioritises and helps remediate vulnerabilities and misconfigurations across an organisation’s assets.
notes.explanation: It covers Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and network devices.
notes.example: Like a building surveyor who ranks every defect by how likely it is to cause harm, and books the repairs.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Security Exposure Management?
notes.back: A solution giving a unified view of security posture across assets and workloads, so you can manage attack surfaces and reduce exposure risk.
notes.explanation: It enriches asset information with security context to protect critical assets proactively.
notes.example: Like a single floor plan marking every door, window and valuable in a building.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender XDR services, “The Microsoft Defender XDR suite”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the Microsoft Defender portal, “Exposure management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.back: Research by Microsoft security researchers on emerging threats, threat actors, campaigns, techniques, vulnerabilities and malware.

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender for Cloud Apps control stops sensitive files being saved to devices the organisation does not manage?
notes.back: Blocking downloads to an unmanaged device.
notes.explanation: It protects data found when scanning connected SaaS apps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “Information protection”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender for Cloud Apps control takes outside people off confidential files?
notes.back: Removing external collaborators.

notes.front: On what are Defender for Cloud Apps’ SSPM recommendations based?
notes.back: Industry standards such as those of the Center for Internet Security, and best practice from each app’s provider.

notes.front: Where does Defender for Cloud Apps automatically surface its SSPM data for supported, connected apps?
notes.back: In Microsoft Secure Score.

notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which two things does app governance in Defender for Cloud Apps watch to keep app hygiene?
notes.back: Unused apps, and current and expired credentials.
notes.explanation: Both help govern the apps used in the organisation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “App to app protection with app governance”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which custom AI agents does Defender for Cloud Apps’ AI agent protection detect?
notes.back: All custom agents created with Microsoft Copilot Studio.
notes.explanation: It watches them for suspicious activity such as prompt injection and can block harmful actions in real time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, “AI agent protection”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where are Defender for Identity’s sensors installed?
notes.back: On on-premises identity servers: domain controllers, and servers running Active Directory Federation Services or Certificate Services.
notes.explanation: The sensors read event logs and network traffic directly from those servers.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does a Defender for Identity sensor send to the Defender for Identity cloud service?
notes.back: Only the parsed information from the logs and network traffic it reads.
notes.explanation: Parsing happens on the sensor, on the server itself.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Defender for Identity help you prevent breaches?
notes.back: By proactively assessing your identity posture.
notes.explanation: For example, it reports sensitive accounts with the riskiest lateral movement paths.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Proactively assess your identity posture”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Defender for Identity detect threats?
notes.back: With real-time analytics and data intelligence, against a behavioural baseline built for each user.
notes.explanation: It flags anomalies from that baseline with adaptive built-in intelligence.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Detect threats, using real-time analytics and data intelligence”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Defender for Identity help you investigate suspicious activity?
notes.back: With clear, actionable incident information, shown as a real-time organisational attack timeline.
notes.explanation: It is designed to cut alert noise and keep only relevant alerts.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Investigate alerts and user activities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Defender for Identity help you respond to attacks?
notes.back: With automatic response to compromised identities.
notes.explanation: It supports remediation actions performed directly on on-premises identities.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender for Identity attack stage covers attackers’ attempts to gather information?
notes.back: Reconnaissance.
notes.explanation: It is the earliest stage in the attack chain Defender for Identity watches.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Detect threats, using real-time analytics and data intelligence”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender for Identity attack stage covers brute force, failed authentications and group membership changes?
notes.back: Compromised credentials.
notes.explanation: These are signs someone is trying to take over user credentials.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Detect threats, using real-time analytics and data intelligence”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender for Identity attack stage covers attempts to move through the network to gain control of sensitive users?
notes.back: Lateral movement.
notes.explanation: The attacker widens control from a first foothold.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Detect threats, using real-time analytics and data intelligence”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Defender for Identity call an attacker gaining control of Active Directory?
notes.back: Domain dominance.
notes.explanation: It can happen through remote code execution on the domain controller, among other methods.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Detect threats, using real-time analytics and data intelligence”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does the Defender for Identity action “disable user in Active Directory” do?
notes.back: It temporarily stops the user signing in to the on-premises network.
notes.explanation: That can stop a compromised user moving laterally or taking data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Remediation actions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does the Defender for Identity action “reset user password” do?
notes.back: It makes the user change their password at the next sign-in.
notes.explanation: The account then cannot be used for further impersonation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Remediation actions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where are Defender for Identity’s security assessments available?
notes.back: From Microsoft Secure Score.
notes.explanation: They add insights for improving security posture and policies.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Microsoft Defender for Identity, “Proactively assess your identity posture”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender Vulnerability Management area uses built-in and agentless scanners to watch for risk, even when devices are off the corporate network?
notes.back: Continuous asset discovery and monitoring.
notes.explanation: Consolidated inventories give a real-time view of software, certificates, hardware, firmware and browser extensions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Continuous asset discovery and monitoring”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender Vulnerability Management area ranks the biggest vulnerabilities using threat intelligence, breach likelihood and business context?
notes.back: Risk-based intelligent prioritisation.
notes.explanation: It gives one view of prioritised recommendations with details such as exposed devices.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Risk-based intelligent prioritization”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender Vulnerability Management area lets security administrators and the wider technology team fix issues together with built-in workflows?
notes.back: Remediation and tracking.
notes.explanation: It includes remediation requests, blocking vulnerable apps and real-time status.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Remediation and tracking”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does risk-based prioritisation in Defender Vulnerability Management treat vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild?
notes.back: It raises the priority of recommendations for them, alongside other emerging threats.
notes.explanation: Prioritisation moves dynamically with what attackers are using now.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Risk-based intelligent prioritization”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Defender Vulnerability Management pinpoint vulnerabilities used in an active breach?
notes.back: By correlating vulnerability management with endpoint detection and response insights.
notes.explanation: A vulnerability being exploited inside the organisation then rises to the top.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Risk-based intelligent prioritization”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which devices does Defender Vulnerability Management treat as high-value assets when prioritising?
notes.back: Exposed devices with business-critical applications, confidential data or high-value users.
notes.explanation: Fixing weaknesses there protects what matters most.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Risk-based intelligent prioritization”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Defender Vulnerability Management send a remediation request to the team that manages devices?
notes.back: By creating a remediation task in Microsoft Intune from a security recommendation.
notes.explanation: Security and device-management teams can then work on the fix together.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Remediation and tracking”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two assessment types Defender Vulnerability Management offers?
notes.back: Any two of, among others: security baselines, browser extensions, digital certificates, hardware and firmware, network shares.
notes.explanation: The certificates assessment, for example, spots certificates before they expire.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “Continuous asset discovery and monitoring”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where in the Defender portal is the Vulnerability Management section now located?
notes.back: Under Exposure management.

notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, “What is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Into which two primary experiences is threat intelligence organised in the Defender portal?
notes.back: Overview and Intel explorer.

notes.back: Reviewing threats relevant to your organisation, such as latest, high-impact and highest-exposure threats.

notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Threat intelligence in Microsoft Defender, “Overview page”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the Defender portal’s threat intelligence, what is Intel explorer for?
notes.back: Searching, filtering and investigating threat intelligence from Microsoft and your own sources.

notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Threat intelligence in Microsoft Defender, “Intel explorer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.back: Any two of: campaigns, indicators, attack patterns, identities, threat actors, tools, vulnerabilities, reports.

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.back: Any two of: discover and monitor assets; get security insights; investigate risk areas with security initiatives; track metrics to improve posture.

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.back: An appropriate Microsoft Entra ID role, such as Global Reader or Administrator, Security Reader or Administrator, or Security Operator.

notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the Microsoft Defender portal, “Describe the Microsoft Defender portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.back: The portal uses role-based access control, so the cards shown depend on the user’s role.

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which incidents appear in the Defender portal’s incidents view?
notes.back: All incidents, including those from the Defender XDR solutions, Microsoft Sentinel and other solutions.

notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the Microsoft Defender portal, “Incidents and alerts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.explanation: An incident also shows its alerts, automated investigations, evidence and response.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe the Microsoft Defender portal, “Incidents and alerts”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two ways to create advanced hunting queries in the Defender portal?
notes.back: Any two of: the query editor using KQL, the query builder, Microsoft Security Copilot from a natural-language request.

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Defender portal node gives access to Microsoft Defender for Cloud?

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An attack starts with a phishing email, then reaches a laptop and a cloud app. The team wants one correlated view across all three. What approach fits?

A) Extended detection and response with Microsoft Defender XDR
B) Cloud security posture management
C) A single endpoint antivirus
D) Azure DDoS Protection

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A college wants to spot attackers probing its on-premises domain controllers. Which Defender XDR product fits?

notes.choices:
A) Microsoft Defender for Office 365
B) Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
C) Microsoft Security Exposure Management
D) Microsoft Defender for Identity

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

A) Attack simulation training
B) The combined incidents queue
C) Safe Links

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

A) Threat analytics reports
B) Advanced hunting
C) Microsoft Secure Score
D) Automatic attack disruption

notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

A) Safe Links
B) Message trace
C) Zero-hour auto purge
D) Safe Attachments

A) Safe Links
B) Attack simulation training
C) Safe Attachments
D) Quarantine policies
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: it trains users rather than scanning links. C is wrong: it inspects files. D is wrong: they define the experience for quarantined messages.

notes.front: A council wants to find which staff would click a phishing email, safely and before a real attack. Which feature fits?

A) Attack simulation training
B) Zero-hour auto purge
C) Threat Explorer

A) Safe Attachments
B) Connection filtering

notes.front: A small team is swamped by routine alerts about well-known threats and wants them investigated and resolved automatically. Which capability fits?

A) Message trace
B) Attack simulation training
C) Automated investigation and response

A) Endpoint detection and response
